There's this huge emphasis on what people should be able to do, but nobody seems to want to take any responsibility for the consequences of their actions. It's just this sociopathic "Oh, I'm hurting them? Sucks to be them then." In reality, we're born with an incredible debt to the people around us and those that came before. Thousands, if not millions work every day to make sure the world we live in keeps on running properly. Countless more made sure it was there to begin with. The least we can do is be a little considerate of the people around us. Before being free as individuals, we need to be free from individuals.

You shouldn't be able to make any little choice that crosses your mind just because, strictly speaking, it's yours to make. Smoking, for example, should not be legal in public spaces. Never mind the children, the ill, and the pregnant- why should I, or anyone else really, be forced to suffer your disgusting habit? Why should the morbidly obese get expensive medical treatment, have entire hospitals refitted, and drive up our healthcare costs because they can't put down the fork? We should sort out the things we can't do before we move on to what we can. If we all just lived a bit more considerately, a bit more efficiently, and more densely, a lot of the bloat in society.

There'll be complaints about commutes, or housing costs, or hell, just how shitty infrastructure is, but I don't recall seeing anyone clamor for denser cities with taller high-rises with new, better planned services. There are things we can all do to make life with other humans a bit more bearable, and make our communities just a little less shitty, but again, it's all about that freedom to do much anything we want without taking responsibility for the bigger picture.
